papers.title: A module-based approach for post-omics, post-GWAS network-based gene classification.
papers.abstract: Complex traits and diseases are highly polygenic and understanding the full set of genes involved is a central challenge in biomedicine. However, due to sample size limitations and noise (technical and biological), experimental approaches for disease-gene discovery such as transcriptomics and GWAS result in long, noisy, heterogeneous gene lists, which may be trimmed to a subset of likely relevant genes while leaving several false negatives. Computational gene classification approaches, especially those using genome-scale molecular interaction networks, are promising avenues for complementing s
papers.summary: This paper presents a module-based computational approach that integrates post-omics and post-GWAS gene lists with molecular interaction networks to classify genes, aiming to reduce noise and recover false negatives in disease-gene discovery. The method leverages network modules to improve gene prioritization for complex traits.

papers.title: Accelerating inference in genomic and proteomic foundation models via speculative decoding.
papers.abstract: Genomic and protein foundation models (GFMs and PFMs) have demonstrated strong performance in learning the language of DNA and proteins, but their use in large-scale sequence generation is limited by the latency of autoregressive decoding. Because every token triggers a forward pass of a large Transformer, whose inference is relatively slow, long-sequence generation quickly becomes costly.
papers.summary: This paper introduces speculative decoding to accelerate inference in genomic and protein foundation models, reducing the latency of autoregressive sequence generation by using a smaller draft model to propose tokens that are then verified in parallel by the large model. This approach speeds up long-sequence generation without compromising output quality, making large-scale genomic and proteomic analyses more practical.

papers.title: Innovative approaches to therapeutic target discovery amid the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance is a constant threat to global public health, requiring innovative strategies for therapeutic target identification. Hence, this narrative review discusses the application of structural modeling and artificial intelligence in the functional prediction of proteins encoded by multidrug-resistant bacterial genomes. Tools such as AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold have enabled high-accuracy three-dimensional structure prediction, facilitating the annotation of hypothetical proteins and the identification of conserved domains and catalytic sites. These computational approaches bridg
papers.summary: This narrative review discusses how structural modeling tools like AlphaFold and RoseTTAFold, combined with artificial intelligence, can predict the functions of proteins from multidrug-resistant bacterial genomes, aiding in the discovery of new therapeutic targets. The authors highlight that these computational methods enable high-accuracy 3D structure prediction, which helps annotate hypothetical proteins and identify conserved domains and catalytic sites relevant to antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Identification of novel HUWE1 variants in Turner-type X-linked intellectual disability.
papers.abstract: To characterize the clinical phenotypes and identify the genetic etiology in four unrelated families affected by Turner-type X-linked intellectual disability (XLID).
papers.summary: This study identifies novel variants in the HUWE1 gene as the genetic cause of Turner-type X-linked intellectual disability in four unrelated families, expanding the known mutational spectrum of this gene. The findings provide a clearer genotype-phenotype correlation and may improve diagnostic accuracy for this condition.

papers.title: SynFlow: an interactive online genome structural variant viewer.
papers.abstract: Structural variations (SVs), including inversions, translocations, duplications, and large insertions or deletions, are key drivers of genome evolution and phenotypic diversity. With the increasing number of high-quality, chromosome-scale genome assemblies, the ability to detect and interpret SVs has become a crucial aspect of modern genomics. While SV detection has advanced, most visualization methods produce static plots that fall short when researchers, particularly in comparative genomics, need to interactively explore large datasets, zoom into specific genomic regions, or dynamically filt
papers.summary: SynFlow is a new interactive online tool for visualizing structural variants (SVs) in genome assemblies, addressing the limitations of static plots by allowing users to zoom, filter, and explore large SV datasets dynamically. This tool is particularly useful for comparative genomics researchers who need to interpret complex genomic rearrangements across multiple high-quality genomes.

papers.title: Evaluation of genomic characteristics of Escherichia coli associated with bovine mastitis and the potential utility of alternative antimicrobial methods.
papers.abstract: Mastitis is a disease that affects dairy cattle and can be caused by multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli, causing losses to the agricultural sector. To address this, research into new substances with antimicrobial activity is crucial. Thus, the objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of extracts of Commiphora leptophloeos, Amburana cearensis, Agave sisalana, and highly soluble polypyrrole (Hs-PPy) against E. coli isolates. Eight E. coli isolates from bovine mastitis and a standard strain were used. The presence of efflux pumps was investigated by ethidium bromide extrusion. Seque
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of microbiology : [publication of the Brazilian Society for Microbiology]
papers.summary: This study evaluated the antimicrobial efficacy of plant extracts and a polypyrrole compound against multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolates from bovine mastitis, and investigated the role of efflux pumps in resistance. The findings suggest these alternative substances may have potential as therapeutic options, though further research is needed.

papers.title: Integrative Bioinformatics and Experimental Validation Reveal that METTL9 Drives Lung Adenocarcinoma Progression via TGF-β/Smad-Mediated EMT Activation.
papers.abstract: Methyltransferase-like 9 (METTL9) has been implicated in tumor progression, yet its clinical significance, functional roles, and immunoregulatory functions in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain unclear. This study aimed to integrate multi-omics datasets and experimental evidence to systematically evaluate the expression profile, prognostic value, molecular mechanisms, and tumor microenvironment (TME)-related functions of METTL9 in LUAD.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with experimental validation to show that METTL9 is upregulated in lung adenocarcinoma and promotes tumor progression by activating the TGF-β/Smad pathway, which drives epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The findings highlight METTL9 as a potential prognostic biomarker and therapeutic target in LUAD.

papers.title: Pansoma, a machine learning tool for identifying somatic variants using pangenome graphs.
papers.abstract: Somatic variant calling, the identification of mutations in non-germline cells acquired over an individual's lifetime, is critical for studying diseases, including cancer, and for developing precision oncology strategies. Traditional somatic variant calling methods rely on linear reference genomes, which do not adequately capture human genetic diversity and result in reference bias, compromising the accuracy of somatic variant detection. Recently developed graph-based human pangenome reference represents diverse genetic variants across human populations and has promised to drive advances in ma
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Pansoma is a new machine learning tool that identifies somatic variants using pangenome graphs, which better capture human genetic diversity than linear reference genomes. By reducing reference bias, it improves the accuracy of somatic variant detection, which is critical for cancer research and precision oncology.

papers.title: MeioBIOME: A snakemake workflow for the parallel analysis of meiofaunal genomes and host-associated bacteria/archaea.
papers.abstract: Microbes closely interact with every living organism, including meiofauna (i.e., microbial eukaryotes 38 μm - 1 mm in length), and influence the development, life cycle, and evolution of diverse metazoans. Together, meiofauna and their microbiomes, collectively referred to as the holobiont, underpin biogeochemical cycles and drive decomposition of organic matter. However, our understanding of the ecological and evolutionary dynamics of meiofauna microbiomes are limited, typically owed to low-resolution 16S rRNA surveys, which cannot accurately delineate bacterial taxa. Single-specimen holobion
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: MeioBIOME is a new Snakemake workflow that enables parallel analysis of meiofaunal genomes and their associated bacteria/archaea, moving beyond low-resolution 16S surveys to provide high-resolution genomic insights into holobiont dynamics. It addresses a gap in studying microbial eukaryotes and their microbiomes, which are important for biogeochemical cycles and organic matter decomposition.

papers.title: EXCAVATE-HT: A Bioinformatic Pipeline to Identify Targetable Genomic Variants for Allele-Specific Editing.
papers.abstract: Allele-specific CRISPR/Cas editing is a powerful tool with great potential for treating genetic diseases and for uncovering the effects of allelic diversity. By targeting commonly inherited single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), a small number of gRNAs can treat many more individuals than targeting rare disease mutations. However, current tools for identifying common targetable variants and generating CRISPR guide RNAs (gRNA) have fundamental conceptual and technical limitations. Here, we introduce EXCAVATE-HT (EXtracting Common Allelic VAriants for Targeted Editing in High-Throughput) a bioi
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EXCAVATE-HT is a new bioinformatic pipeline that identifies common, targetable SNPs for allele-specific CRISPR editing, overcoming limitations of existing tools. It enables a small set of gRNAs to treat many individuals by leveraging common variants, with potential applications in genetic disease therapy and functional studies of allelic diversity.

papers.title: HPRC2: A human pangenome reference with near-complete coverage of common genetic variation.
papers.abstract: A pangenome reference overcomes the inherent limitation of any individual reference genome by integrating the variation present in a population. We present the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium's (HPRC) Release 2 (HPRC2), an openly available, second phase pangenome that is an approximately fivefold expansion in genome number over HPRC Release 1 (HPRC1) and measurable improvement in genome completeness, contiguity, and accuracy. Selecting samples with a principled algorithm prioritising common variant coverage, HPRC2 contributes 460 haplotypes that together capture over 99% of common variati
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: HPRC2 is a new human pangenome reference from the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium, expanding to 460 haplotypes—about five times more than the first release—with improved completeness, contiguity, and accuracy. It captures over 99% of common genetic variation, addressing a key limitation of single reference genomes.

papers.title: Gene model for the ortholog of raptor in Drosophila eugracilis.
papers.abstract: Gene model for the ortholog of raptor in the D. eugracilis Apr. 2013 (BCM-HGSC/Deug_2.0) (DeugGB2) Genome Assembly (GenBank Accession: GCA_000236325.2) of Drosophila eugracilis. This ortholog was characterized as part of a developing dataset to study the evolution of the Insulin/insulin-like growth factor signaling pathway (IIS) across the genus Drosophila using the Genomics Education Partnership gene annotation protocol for Course-based Undergraduate Research Experiences.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint presents a gene model for the raptor ortholog in Drosophila eugracilis, annotated as part of a course-based undergraduate research project. The work contributes a detailed annotation for studying the evolution of the insulin/IGF signaling pathway across Drosophila species.

papers.title: Uniform processing and analysis of IGVF massively parallel reporter assay data with MPRAsnakeflow.
papers.abstract: As researchers and clinicians seek to identify human genomic alterations relevant to traits and disorders, identifying and aggregating evidence providing mechanistic support for associations between alterations and phenotypes remains challenging. In particular, the study of noncoding genomic variation remains a major challenge because of the lack of accurate functional annotation for activity in a given context and across alleles. Experimental evidence is critical for prioritizing and interpreting functional effects of genetic alterations. Massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs) have emerge
papers.summary: This paper presents MPRAsnakeflow, a standardized computational pipeline for uniformly processing and analyzing massively parallel reporter assay (MPRA) data from the Impact of Genomic Variation on Function (IGVF) consortium. The pipeline addresses the challenge of inconsistent data processing across studies, enabling more reliable integration and interpretation of functional genomic evidence for noncoding variants.

papers.title: An alignment-free strategy for circulating tumor DNA detection and tumor fraction estimation from whole-genome sequencing data.
papers.abstract: Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is emerging as a promising biomarker for postoperative monitoring of cancer patients. Precise estimation of circulating tumor fraction is crucial for evaluating treatment effects and timely detection of disease recurrence. All current ctDNA detection methods that utilize whole-genome sequencing (WGS) data rely on the reference genome alignment of sequencing reads and often apply separate tools for detecting different variant types. However, various bioinformatic analysis confounders and the application of external variant calling tools could be avoided by analyzin
papers.summary: This paper presents a new alignment-free method for detecting circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and estimating tumor fraction directly from whole-genome sequencing data, bypassing the need for reference genome alignment and external variant callers. By avoiding alignment, the approach reduces bioinformatic confounders and simplifies the analysis pipeline, potentially improving accuracy and speed for postoperative cancer monitoring.

papers.title: Lineage-associated small inversions disrupt dosT, dnaE2, and a promoter-adjacent region in some Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.
papers.abstract: Large molecular inversions in the genome of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) due to factors like the presence of insertion sequences and transposases are widely known. However, smaller inversions within coding sequences and non-coding control elements are rarely reported. The present study aims to identify inversions and their potential impact on Mtb biology in a lineage-specific manner. Structural variants (SVs) could only be detected by long reads. For this, we simulated long reads by de novo assembling the short-read sequencing data sets and subsequently aligned representative strains from
papers.summary: This study identifies small genomic inversions in Mycobacterium tuberculosis that disrupt the dosT, dnaE2 genes and a promoter-adjacent region, and shows these inversions are lineage-associated. Using simulated long reads from short-read data, the authors demonstrate that such structural variants can be detected and may impact Mtb biology in a lineage-specific manner.

papers.title: hypeR-GEM: connecting metabolite signatures to enzyme-coding genes via genome-scale metabolic models.
papers.abstract: Enrichment analysis is a cornerstone of "omics" data interpretation, enabling researchers to connect analysis results to biological processes and generate testable hypotheses. Enrichment analysis in metabolomics poses distinct challenges for interpretation and multi-omics integration due to the lack of well-defined and consistent connections to well-curated gene-centered biological knowledge repositories. To address these challenges, we developed hypeR-GEM, a methodology and associated R package that adapts gene set enrichment analysis to metabolomics. hypeR-GEM leverages genome-scale metaboli
papers.summary: hypeR-GEM is a new R package that adapts gene set enrichment analysis for metabolomics by using genome-scale metabolic models to connect metabolite signatures to enzyme-coding genes. This enables better interpretation of metabolomics data and facilitates integration with other omics data types.

papers.title: Draft genome sequence of the almond red leaf blotch pathogen Polystigma amygdalinum assembled from infected almond leaves collected in California, USA.
papers.abstract: We report a draft genome assembly of Polystigma amygdalinum, the causal agent of almond red leaf blotch. DNA extracted from infected leaves was sequenced using PacBio HiFi, and host-derived reads were removed bioinformatically. The 238.7-Mb assembly (90.8% BUSCO completeness) is highly repetitive (82.3%) and unusually large for an ascomycete.
papers.summary: This paper reports the first draft genome assembly of Polystigma amygdalinum, the fungus causing almond red leaf blotch, assembled from infected leaf tissue using PacBio HiFi sequencing. The genome is unusually large (238.7 Mb) and highly repetitive (82.3%) for an ascomycete, with 90.8% BUSCO completeness, providing a valuable resource for studying this pathogen's biology and evolution.

papers.title: DeepGeSeq: Deep learning library for Genomic Sequence modeling and analysis.
papers.abstract: Deep learning methods have demonstrated significant potential in genomics, enabling broad applications such as sequence activity prediction, regulatory rule identification, and variant effect quantification. However, their widespread adoption is often hindered by the steep computational learning curve required for model construction, training, and downstream biological interpretation. Here, we introduce DeepGeSeq, a user-friendly Deep-learning library tailored for Genomic Sequence modeling and analysis.
papers.summary: DeepGeSeq is a user-friendly deep learning library designed to lower the barrier for applying deep learning to genomic sequence analysis, covering tasks like sequence activity prediction, regulatory rule identification, and variant effect quantification. It aims to simplify model construction, training, and biological interpretation for researchers.

papers.title: AniAnn's: alignment-free annotation of tandem repeat arrays using fast average nucleotide identity estimates.
papers.abstract: Satellite DNA has long posed challenges for genome assembly and analysis due to its low sequence complexity and poor mappability. These large heterochromatic arrays of tandem repeats are ubiquitous across eukaryotic genomes, yet remain understudied. Current methods for annotating satellite regions, and other classes of tandem repeat arrays, are limited in their ability to annotate divergent or novel sequences.
papers.summary: AniAnn's is a new alignment-free tool that annotates tandem repeat arrays (like satellite DNA) by using fast average nucleotide identity estimates, overcoming limitations of existing methods for divergent or novel sequences. This addresses the challenge of studying these repetitive, hard-to-assemble genomic regions.

papers.title: map3C: a computational tool for processing multiomic single-cell Hi-C data.
papers.abstract: The emergence of multiomic single-cell Hi-C (scHi-C) methods, which simultaneously profile chromatin conformation and other modalities such as gene expression or DNA methylation, creates tremendous opportunities for studying the genome's structure-function relationships. Existing tools for processing multiomic scHi-C datasets lack certain key functions for downstream bioinformatics analysis. We present map3C, a software tool that incorporates additional key functions. Specifically, we demonstrate that map3C facilitates multiomic scHi-C processing, quality control, and identification of structu
papers.summary: map3C is a new computational tool that processes multiomic single-cell Hi-C data, adding key functions for quality control and identification of structural features that existing tools lack. It enables researchers to better analyze chromatin conformation alongside other modalities like gene expression or DNA methylation.

papers.title: The Clinical Phenotype and Genetic Analysis of Monogenic Non Syndromic Obesity Caused by MC4R Gene Variation.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to investigate the clinical features and genetic variation of a patient with monogenic nonsyndromic obesity caused by melanocortin 4 receptor (MC4R) gene variation. Additionally, this study aims to provide a reference for the diagnosis of the disease.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the clinical phenotype and genetic basis of monogenic non-syndromic obesity caused by a variation in the MC4R gene, providing diagnostic insights for this rare form of obesity. The findings contribute to understanding the genotype-phenotype correlation in MC4R-related obesity.

papers.title: Drug sensitivity prediction across cancer types using graph isomorphism networks and biological pathway features: A dual-branch deep learning approach.
papers.abstract: Drug sensitivity prediction is an important issue within the precision medicine field. IC50, which is the molar drug dose needed to decrease the viability of cells by half compared to the drug-free control, is the main pharmacodynamics parameter used for drug sensitivity analysis in large-scale pharmacogenomics screenings. Computational estimation of IC50s based on molecular and genomic factors significantly reduces costs associated with experiments for measuring cell viability and allows for accelerating the process of drug discovery. Traditional methods of IC50 calculation do not allow integ
papers.summary: This study presents a dual-branch deep learning model that combines graph isomorphism networks with biological pathway features to predict drug sensitivity (IC50) across cancer types. The approach improves prediction accuracy by integrating molecular and genomic data, offering a cost-effective computational alternative to experimental drug sensitivity measurements.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in haematology laboratory diagnosis: Current applications, challenges, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming haematology diagnostics by improving accuracy, efficiency, and reproducibility in workflows traditionally reliant on manual microscopy and expert interpretation. Integrating AI into laboratory medicine presents opportunities to enhance diagnostic precision and reduce variability, particularly in resource-limited settings.
papers.summary: This review examines the current applications, challenges, and future directions of artificial intelligence in haematology laboratory diagnosis, highlighting its potential to improve accuracy, efficiency, and reproducibility in workflows that traditionally depend on manual microscopy. It emphasizes opportunities for enhancing diagnostic precision and reducing variability, particularly in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Barrier-to-Autointegration Factor 1: a key regulator of nuclear envelope integrity, genome stability, and disease progression.
papers.abstract: Barrier-to-Autointegration Factor 1 (BANF1) is a self-associating protein encoded within the q13.1 locus of chromosome 11. It is integral to multiple cellular processes, including cell cycle regulation, chromatin organization, gene expression modulation, nuclear envelope (NE) repair, DNA damage repair (DDR), innate immune function, and viral infection control. While prior investigations have provided preliminary phenotypic and bioinformatic characterizations of BANF1 across various disease states, comprehensive analyses detailing its functional roles and mechanistic underpinnings in diverse pa
papers.summary: This review consolidates current knowledge on Barrier-to-Autointegration Factor 1 (BANF1), a protein critical for nuclear envelope integrity, genome stability, and immune function. It highlights BANF1's roles in chromatin organization, DNA damage repair, and viral infection control, and discusses its implications in disease progression, though it notes that comprehensive mechanistic analyses across diseases are still lacking.

papers.title: Structural Genomics Defines PBRM1 Bromodomain Variant Function in ccRCC.
papers.abstract: Polybromo-1 (PBRM1) modulates chromatin accessibility and transcription via six bromodomains that bind acetyl-lysine residues on nuclear proteins. PBRM1 variants exist in ~40% of clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) cases. PBRM1 loss correlates with improved responses to antiangiogenics and immune checkpoint blockade, which are the standard of care for ccRCC therapy. Missense variants cluster within PBRM1 bromodomains and are present in 16% of ccRCC cases, with unknown impacts on therapeutic response. Since in-depth biophysical and cellular testing of the hundreds of PBRM1 missense variants
papers.summary: This study uses structural genomics to functionally characterize PBRM1 bromodomain missense variants found in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC), revealing how specific mutations affect acetyl-lysine binding and chromatin regulation. The findings provide a framework for interpreting variant pathogenicity and potential therapeutic response, which is clinically relevant given PBRM1's role in ccRCC treatment outcomes.

papers.title: Targeting NOP14 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment and enhances the antitumor efficacy of PD-1 blockade in DLBCL.
papers.abstract: Nucleolar Protein 14 (NOP14), a highly conserved factor in eukaryotes, is essential for pre-18S rRNA processing and small ribosomal subunit assembly. Emerging evidence underscores its pivotal regulatory role in the progression of various malignancies. Nevertheless, its functional involvement in Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), particularly its capacity to modulate the tumor immune microenvironment, remains to be fully elucidated.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of NOP14 in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and finds that targeting NOP14 remodels the tumor immune microenvironment, enhancing the antitumor efficacy of PD-1 blockade. The findings suggest NOP14 as a potential therapeutic target to improve immunotherapy outcomes in DLBCL.

papers.title: Unveiling the aging-immune axis in irritable bowel syndrome: a multi-omics and machine learning approach to biomarker discovery and validation.
papers.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a prevalent functional gastrointestinal disorder with an elusive pathophysiology. Although immune dysregulation and mild mucosal inflammation are recognized as important factors in IBS, the specific contribution of immunosenescence remains unclear. Prior MR studies on IBS focused on single molecular traits; however, an integrated multi-omics framework for aging-immune genes has not been applied. Here, we integrate cis-eQTL/pQTL/mQTL with machine learning and in vivo validation to identify putatively causal biomarkers and unravel the aging-immune axis.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data (eQTL, pQTL, mQTL) with machine learning to identify aging-related immune biomarkers for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and validates findings in vivo. It reveals a potential aging-immune axis contributing to IBS pathophysiology, offering new candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Integrating genomic structural equation modeling and experimental validation to unravel the genetic basis of male genital lichen sclerosus.
papers.abstract: To investigate the genetic architecture of male genital lichen sclerosus (MGLSc) and to identify potential susceptibility loci, candidate genes, and biological pathways associated with disease pathogenesis by integrating genomic structural equation modeling (Genomic-SEM) with multi-omics analyses and experimental validation.
papers.summary: This study integrates genomic structural equation modeling with multi-omics data and experimental validation to uncover the genetic architecture of male genital lichen sclerosus, identifying potential susceptibility loci, candidate genes, and biological pathways. The findings provide new insights into the pathogenesis of this condition and highlight promising targets for further investigation.

papers.title: Clinically interpretable deep learning for breast cancer missense variant pathogenicity prediction.
papers.abstract: Missense variants in breast cancer remain diagnostically challenging due to their functional diversity and complex genomic contexts. Conventional laboratory assays for evaluating pathogenicity are labor-intensive, costly, and often impractical for large-scale screening, creating a pressing need for accurate, scalable, and clinically interpretable computational approaches.
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning model that predicts the pathogenicity of missense variants in breast cancer, designed to be clinically interpretable. The model offers a scalable alternative to labor-intensive laboratory assays, addressing the need for accurate computational screening tools.

papers.title: Novel variants of TP63 identified in Chinese families with split-hand/foot malformation.
papers.abstract: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) is a group of congenital birth defects affecting the hands and feet, significantly impairing patients quality of life. The TP63 gene encodes the p63 protein, heterozygous TP63 variants can cause SHFM. The aim of this study was to identify TP63 gene variants in three Chinese families with SHFM.
papers.summary: This study identified novel TP63 gene variants in three Chinese families with split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM), a congenital limb defect. The findings expand the known mutational spectrum of TP63 associated with SHFM and may aid in genetic diagnosis and counseling for affected families.
